items.title: Last night an AI agent performed brain surgery on a mouse
items.summary: An AI agent successfully performed brain surgery on a mouse, showcasing the potential of AI in complex medical procedures. This development could pave the way for future applications of AI in surgery, significantly impacting the medical field.

items.title: Supermarket freezers across Europe hit by second suspected cyber-attack
items.summary: A second suspected cyber-attack has targeted supermarket freezers across Europe, raising concerns about the security of critical infrastructure. Developers and engineers should be aware of the vulnerabilities in operational technology systems and the implications for cybersecurity.

items.title: Mystery of 60-Second Fluctuations in Power Grids Solved
items.summary: Researchers have uncovered the cause of 60-second fluctuations in power grids, which could lead to improved stability and efficiency in energy distribution. This finding is crucial for engineers working on smart grid technologies and energy management systems.

items.title: Postgres 19 is late because so many more bugs are being found now
items.summary: The release of Postgres 19 has been delayed due to an increase in the number of bugs being discovered during the testing phase. This highlights the importance of thorough testing and quality assurance in open-source projects, which developers should prioritize.

items.title: Nibnib: Image compression with extreme decompression speed
items.summary: Nibnib is a new image compression tool that boasts extremely fast decompression speeds, making it ideal for applications requiring quick access to images. Developers in web engineering and application development should consider integrating this tool to enhance performance.
